questions.q: 'The captain, as well as the players, ___ (was/were) congratulated.'
questions.a: 'was' — 'as well as' is a parenthetical insert, not a coordinator; subject stays singular. A wrong answer 'were' reveals the student believes as-well-as = and, the exact misconception this node exists to kill.

questions.q: 'There ___ (is/are) a boy and two girls waiting outside.'
questions.a: 'are' — compound subject 'a boy and two girls' follows the verb. (Some accept proximity 'is'; boards expect 'are'.) A wrong answer 'is' chosen because 'a boy' is singular shows the student applied proximity logic to the one construction where it is explicitly wrong.

What is Subject–verb agreement? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Subject–verb agreement is decided by the HEAD of the subject phrase, never by the noun nearest the verb. 'The box of chocolates is empty' — 'box' is the head, 'chocolates' is a prepositional decoy.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Subject–verb agreement?
questions.a: Students agree the verb with the nearest noun ('the box of chocolates are') — proximity agreement — and treat 'as well as / along with' like 'and', wrongly pluralizing the subject.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can identify the head noun in a subject phrase of any length, strip intervening phrases (of-, with-, along with-, as well as-), and choose the correct verb form in 9/10 items including inverted and there-sentences.
